newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu's soldier son Kongolo flees Zaire to Congo.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's soldier son Kongolo flees Zaire to Congo.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko's soldier son Captain Kongolo Mobutu arrived in Congo on Saturday after fleeing Zaire's capital on board a speedboat with about 20 other men, witnesses said.

Kongolo, an officer in Mobutu's presidential guard, arrived in Congo's capital Brazzaville as reports from across the Zaire River in Kinshasa spoke of Laurent Kabila's rebels arriving in the outskirts of the Zairean capital.
Zaire's veteran president, fighting cancer and seven months of civil war, stepped aside on Friday and left Kinshasa for his jungle palace in his home region of Gbadolite.
A source at the presidency in Kinshasa said he understood that Mobutu was still there on Saturday.

Witnesses said Congolese security forces closely checked Kongolo and the other new arrivals. Those on board the boat handed weapons to Congolese police in riot gear who surrounded them, the witnesses added.
Kongolo and his companions were not wearing military uniform. Kongolo wore a green T-shirt.
The source at the presidency in Kinshasa and other sources in the city said that members of Mobutu's armed forces were fleeing west on the road out of the city to lower Zaire.
Earlier, Congo closed its river border with Zaire to passenger traffic, fearing a flood of Kinshasa residents.
"The river border has been closed to avoid any disorderly movement of Zaireans leaving the other side," said Raoul Zatonga, an official at the Interior Ministry said.

Only one ferry and a handful of private speedboats were seen attempting to cross the Zaire River on Saturday. The river is about five km (three miles) wide at the point where it separates Brazzaville from the Zairean capital Kinshasa.
River traffic has been interrupted in recent days because of strikes by immigration officials in Kinshasa, but this is the first border closure decided by the Congolese authorities.
U.S., French, British, Belgian and Portuguese troops were on standby in Brazzaville to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa if need be.
